name: SLU-PP-332

lead: SLU-PP-332 is an experimental compound that activates estrogen-related receptors and, in mice, produced an exercise-like response and better running capacity.
Studies are limited to mice and cells, and no human results are published.

paras: It activates ERR alpha, beta and gamma, receptors that control mitochondrial and fat metabolism in muscle.
Human safety is unknown. It is not an approved drug, and doping-control methods for it have been published.

Novel ERR pan-agonists ameliorate heart failure through boosting cardiac fatty acid metabolism and mitochondrial function

lead: SLU-PP-332 is an experimental synthetic agonist of the estrogen-related receptors (ERR alpha, beta and gamma), described by its developers as an exercise mimetic because it triggered an exercise-like gene program and increased running capacity in mice.[1][2]

Published results come from mice and cell studies, including models of metabolic syndrome, heart failure and kidney aging.[3][4][5] No human trial results have been published. Anti-doping laboratories have published methods for detecting it.[6][7]

paras: SLU-PP-332 activates ERR alpha, beta and gamma, nuclear receptors that regulate mitochondrial and fatty acid metabolism in muscle and heart. A 2023 study reported that it induced an ERR-alpha-dependent acute aerobic exercise response in mice.[1]

In mice it enhanced exercise capacity,[1] and in a mouse model of metabolic syndrome it was reported to improve metabolic parameters.[4] Related pan-ERR agonists were reported to improve cardiac metabolism in heart failure models,[2] and the compound reversed mitochondrial dysfunction and inflammation in aging mouse kidney.[3] A 2025 pilot study examined ERR targeting for age-related muscle atrophy from inactivity.[5] Chemical optimization work and a related compound, SLU-PP-915, have been reported.[8][9]
No studies found. All published research is in cells and animals.

Analytical chemists have published in vitro metabolism studies of SLU-PP-332 for doping control, describing it as having doping potential.[6][7] It is sold online as a research compound and is not approved as a medicine.
